analysis.question: four ways to put 400 chains on four GPUs, and whether two pmaps over disjoint device pairs overlap

the_protocol_confirmed.finding: B (two waves of 4x51 and 4x49) beats A (one wave of 4x100) by 16.8% on real hardware
the_protocol_confirmed.note: first direct multi-GPU confirmation of the split protocol

the_uneven_split_fails.proposal: 2x101 on two GPUs and 2x99 on the other two, one wave
the_uneven_split_fails.why_it_should_work: each device gets about 100 chains, odd so width 1, and out of the steep part of the a/B curve -- strictly better than 25 per device and no worse than 51
the_uneven_split_fails.measured: C costs 0.0836 s against B's 0.0455, which is +83.8%
the_uneven_split_fails.diagnosis: THE TWO PMAPS DO NOT OVERLAP. Each uses only two of the four devices, so if they serialise the scheme runs on half the hardware for twice as long, which is what the roughly +84% says. The idea is sound; the runtime does not deliver the concurrency it needs.

the_25_finding.claim: BP + replicas on 4 GPUs shards 100 chains into 25 per device, which the production f(B) curve puts at 11.561 s/replica against 9.130 at B=45 and 9.162 at B=55 -- 26% worse
the_25_finding.status: CONFIRMED from the measured curve, and it explains why 'both' beats 'replicas' on 4 GPUs despite paying the width-4 penalty

analysis.honest_caveat: This ran at 400 sweeps, where the a/B curve does not reproduce the production ranking: scheme D (4x25) came out at +6.7% against A here while the production-extrapolated model puts it at -9.9%. So the MAGNITUDES here do not transfer to the full ladder. What does transfer is the structural finding, that disjoint pmaps serialise, since that is a property of the dispatch rather than of the schedule.
